chains.title: Alt T reduces TCF7L2 binding and derepresses POU5F1B
chains.cell_type: HCT116 colorectal carcinoma and colon transverse expression context

links.claim: TCF7L2 is expressed in HCT116 (63.61 TPM; E05), has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT116 (E05), and QBiC-SELEX HMG/Sox models detect allele-specific binding with ref G binding more strongly than alt T (best LEF1-mapped model effect -0.47, z -4.66; E20/E35). E43 shows LEF1 has the same own model and comparable effect, so the motif is HMG/Sox but TCF7L2-specific attribution remains ambiguous.

The variant lies in EH38E3858447, a proximal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase, H3K27ac and CTCF signal, and VEP annotates an enhancer at the site. The chromatin z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, so HCT116-specific activity is inferred rather than directly shown.

This chain uses POU5F1B as the target because the colon-transverse eQTL shows alt T associated with higher POU5F1B (NES +0.20; E17/E38) and POU5F1B has the best L2G score at the locus (0.89; E16). The mechanism requires TCF7L2 to repress POU5F1B, so that loss of TCF7L2 binding on alt T derepresses POU5F1B. E41 found only co-mentions of TCF7L2 and colorectal cancer/Wnt signaling, not a direct TCF7L2-POU5F1B regulatory report or perturbation; the repressor step remains an assumption.

TCF7L2 occupancy over the variant is shown in the matching HCT116 biosample (E05), and the POU5F1B eQTL is significant in colon transverse (E38). The occupancy and colon expression contexts align, but no HCT116 POU5F1B perturbation or allele-specific reporter is cited.

The T allele is the strongest colorectal cancer risk allele at this locus (p 2.0e-122; E15), and POU5F1B has the best L2G score (E16) with substantial Open Targets colorectal-cancer association (overall 0.54, genetic_association 0.87; E42). However, POU5F1B is not a CRISPR dependency in HCT116 or bowel lineage (E37), and E15 reports G as the effect allele for several other colorectal/colon traits, so phenotype mediation remains unproven and direction is not uniform across trait definitions.

TCF7L2 depletion in HCT116 does not increase POU5F1B or does not mimic the alt T allele.
An MPRA/reporter shows no alt-T-dependent enhancer change or shows that mutation of the TCF7L2 site does not alter the allelic effect.

The chain's decision link is the assumption that TCF7L2 represses POU5F1B and that losing its site on T derepresses it. Nothing cited speaks to the sign of TCF7L2 action at this element (TCF7L2/TCF4 is canonically a Wnt/β-catenin activator); plus the L2G support (E16) is dominated by prostate/PSA credible sets whose reported effect allele is G, the opposite of the CRC/colon eQTL allele, and POU5F1B is 78.9 kb away. Gene assignment is supported, the mechanism is not.

EH38E3858447 is a pELS with DNase (z 5.2), H3K27ac (z 4.8) and CTCF (z 4.1), and VEP calls an enhancer at the site, so element identity is supported. But the z-scores are maxima over all ENCODE biosamples with no HCT116-specific value, so an active element in colorectal cells is inferred, and these rows say nothing about allele-specificity of the element.

TCF7L2 is expressed at 63.61 TPM (rank 53/1626) and has 4 ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks over the variant in HCT116; E04 confirms HCT116 is among the assayed biosamples with peaks at this element. Colon transverse eQTL is a colorectal epithelial context. Cell-type matching is directly shown.

The T allele being the CRC risk allele at p 2.0e-122 (E15) is solid, but the proposed causal route (TCF7L2-dependent derepression of POU5F1B → CRC risk) is supported only by title-level literature (E18: circRNA sponging, ecDNA, CCAT2 review) that never shows POU5F1B as the causal gene at this locus or links TCF7L2 to it. The same variant is the top PSA/prostate signal with the opposite effect allele, i.e. pleiotropy is not addressed.

E29 gives a real QBiC change in the claimed direction (z 20.82, effect 1.92, alt>ref, alt site at 100th percentile), but it comes from a CIS-BP-mapped NR2F6 model, not an NR2F2 model, and the identical z/effect (20.82 / 1.92) reappears unchanged for NR1D1 (E33) and NR1D2 (E34). second.reason: Chain A (H0 null) is a link-free hypothesis and gets no positive support from any cited row: nothing tests allele-specific occupancy at this base, nothing tests enhancer activity of the G>T base alone, and no linked causal variant or non-TF mechanism is shown. Its central prediction ('no allele-specific TF occupancy / no TF-mediated effect') is in fact leaned against, though not refuted, by rows showing dense TF occupancy over the variant in the matching biosample (E04: 330 peaks, 10 peaks from 9 factors in HCT116; E05-E11) and by QBiC-SELEX alleles passing the gate at occupied sites (E20 TCF7L2 z -4.66; E21 SRF z -7.74; E22 SP1 z -4.76). None of this is allele-specific occupancy in cells, so it cannot score as 'supported' — but it means the null is not positively supported either; its predictions are 'not tested', which counts for neither chain. Chain B, by contrast, has a real, cell-type-matched anchor: SP1 is expressed in HCT116 and has an ENCODE ChIP-seq peak over the variant in HCT116 (E06), and QBiC-SELEX reports a gate-passing change in the claimed direction, ref G binding more (effect -0.211, z -4.76; E22), with the element annotated as an active pELS containing the variant (E01, E03). That binding link is weak, not supported, because the change comes from an SP4-mapped model rather than SP1's own model and the site is weak at both alleles, with the evidence text itself saying the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element. The downstream links are weaker still and are correctly flagged: element activity in HCT116 is inferred from biosample maxima (E03); the gene link rests on a whole-blood CASC8 eQTL with alt T lowering CASC8 (NES -0.32; E17), with no CASC8 colon eQTL (E38) and no SP1-CASC8 perturbation; and the phenotype link is thin (CASC8 Open Targets CRC score 0.02; E40) even though the T allele is the CRC risk allele (E15). Direction is internally consistent across B (ref binds more -> alt lowers CASC8 -> T is risk allele), but CASC8 is a second-choice target when POU5F1B carries the L2G and colon eQTL evidence (E16, E17, E38, E42), so B over-reaches on the gene rather than on the binding. Even discounting that, B's binding link has direct occupancy in the right cell type plus a directional SELEX change, while A has no direct evidence at all. One test cuts mildly against B's gene link — CASC8 is not an eQTL in Colon_Transverse (E38) — but that is a GTEx tissue, not HCT116, and it does not amount to a demonstrated absence of TF effect, which is what the null asserts. The evidence therefore separates the chains only weakly, and in favor of B.
